edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Abscond (shield-dash) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Viktor Gravity Field (W): 17s at rank 1 — the stun zone owns every all-in. The moment it drops you own a full window to chain in; otherwise fight outside it. - Hextech Ray (E) is 12s early — step up right after he wastes it. - Your R goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: E-shield in, E2-chain, Q-W with whirls between, heal out — the full brawl string he answered with one rotation and regret.
edits.after: Arcane Storm is a 120-second teamfight tool — steal it early and you cast it twice before he ever sees his own come back up.

edits.before: Chaining into a loaded CC with W down — Sylas without the heal is a mage who chose melee for the aesthetic.
edits.after: A hoarded Hijack is a dead summoner — a stolen Arcane Storm spent on a pick or crash beats the perfect fight that never comes.

edits.before: That’s Viktor’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 turn into a skill matchup once his E Death Ray is upgraded: he can poke and zone with the laser, so you must dodge it and pick your all-in around his W Gravity Field cooldown. Bait the Q shield, E Abscond in, and finish with W Kingslayer whenever his stun zone is down.

edits.before: This is a scaling loss: a two-item Viktor with Chaos Storm, upgraded Death Ray, and Gravity Field controls fights in a way your single-target dive cannot answer. Your job is to convert the early and level-6 leads into objectives and end before he comes fully online. In the late game, group with your team and hunt Abduct picks rather than dueling him through his zone control.
